title: Separation descends under universally closed surjections of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and atlas point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A space is quasi-compact if every open cover of its point space has a finite subcover, and quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. A morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback to every affine scheme test has quasi-compact source, and quasi-separated if its relative diagonal is quasi-compact. Let $f:X\to Y$ be surjective on point spaces and universally closed, meaning that every algebraic-space base change induces a closed map on point spaces [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. If $X$ is quasi-separated, then $Y$ is quasi-separated. If the absolute diagonal of $X$ is a closed immersion, then the absolute diagonal of $Y$ is a closed immersion as well; here closed immersions are representable and closed immersions on scheme tests [def-weil-closed-immersion]. No finite type or Noetherian hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] to regard $X,Y$ as spaces over $B=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. The same scheme atlases give the same point spaces and topology. Any space $T\to Y$ over $B$ acquires an $S$-structure through $Y\to S$, and the equivalence and fibre-product assertion identify $X\times_YT$ with its original $S$-space fibre product. Thus universal closedness of $f$ still holds for all these tests. The hypotheses on the absolute diagonals are exactly those in the question; no identification with the relative diagonals over $S$ is made.

source.place: Tag 05Z2, reduction of (1),(2) to (3),(4) over Spec Z; change of base is spaces.tex Tags 03I4 and 04SG.

proof.text: Write $A=X\times_BX$, $C=Y\times_BY$, and $F=f\times_Bf:A\to C$. Factor $F$ as $X\times_BX\to X\times_BY\to Y\times_BY$. The two factors are base changes of $f$, on the second and first coordinates respectively. For any further base change each is closed by the definition of universal closedness, and their composite is closed because the image of a closed set under the first map and then the second is closed. Hence $F$ is universally closed. The equality $F\Delta_X=\Delta_Yf$ follows by comparing the two projections of the sheaf fibre products.

source.place: Tag 05Z2, first diagram and paragraph; Tags 03IS and 03IU, elementary base-change and composition arguments.

proof.text: For any algebraic space $T\to C$, set $P=T\times_CA$, $R=T\times_CX$, and $Q=T\times_CY$, where $X\to C$ is $F\Delta_X$ and $Y\to C$ is $\Delta_Y$. Then $R=P\times_AX$ and $R=Q\times_YX$: both equalities follow sectionwise by retaining the same coordinates and their equalities. Thus $R\to Q$ is a base change of $f$. By the point-fibre-product surjectivity in [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], $|R|\to|Q|$ is surjective. The same node gives continuity of every point map. This uses surjectivity on point spaces, without assuming that $f$ is representable.

source.place: Tag 05Z2, both test-space arguments; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03H4 (lemma-points-cartesian).

proof.text: Assume $X$ is quasi-separated and take $T$ affine. By [lem-sfb-space-universally-closed-quasicompact] applied to $F$, $P$ is quasi-compact. Choose an affine surjective etale atlas $U\to P$ by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]. Since $\Delta_X$ is quasi-compact, $U\times_AX$ is quasi-compact. It maps onto $R=P\times_AX$ on point spaces, by the base-change point-surjectivity from [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. The continuous images $|U\times_AX|\twoheadrightarrow|R|\twoheadrightarrow|Q|$ are quasi-compact: pull back an open covering, choose a finite subcover, and use surjectivity. Consequently every affine test $Q$ of $\Delta_Y$ is quasi-compact, proving that $Y$ is quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 05Z2, first medskip paragraph, with the compact-source reduction expanded using spaces-properties.tex Tag 03H6.

proof.text: Now assume $\Delta_X$ is a closed immersion. By [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper] it is universally closed. The composition argument of step 2 shows $F\Delta_X$ is universally closed. For arbitrary $T\to C$ retain step 3: $h:R\to T$ is universally closed and $p:R\to Q$ is surjective on points. If $E\subseteq|Q|$ is closed, continuity of $|p|$ makes $|p|^{-1}(E)$ closed, so its image under $|h|$ is closed in $|T|$. Surjectivity identifies this image with the image of $E$ under $|Q|\to|T|$. Thus $Q\to T$ is closed for every algebraic-space test $T$, and $\Delta_Y$ is universally closed.

source.place: Tag 05Z2, second medskip paragraph: universal closedness of the target diagonal, with closed-set cancellation written explicitly.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-diagonal-scheme-tests] to $Y\to B$. For every scheme $T\to C$, its diagonal test $d:D=Y\times_CT\to T$ is a scheme morphism, locally of finite type and a monomorphism. Step 5 makes $d$ universally closed, in particular after all scheme base changes. It is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-universally-closed-quasi-compact] and separated by [lem-trf-scheme-monomorphism-separated]. Thus it is of finite type (local finite type plus quasi-compact) and proper by the scheme definitions [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. The equivalence [lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed] makes $d$ a closed immersion. This holds for every scheme test and the diagonal is representable, so $\Delta_Y$ is a closed immersion, as required.

source.place: Tag 05Z2, final paragraph; Tag 03HK (lemma-properties-diagonal), parts (1)-(3); etale.tex Tag 04XV (lemma-characterize-closed-immersion), (1),(2),(6).

Step 5 gets universal closedness of Δ_Y from the closed-immersion-is-proper node by closed-set cancellation, against all space tests. Step 6 combines the diagonal scheme-test node with Mathlib leaves 04XU, isSeparated_of_mono and IsClosedImmersion.iff_isProper_and_mono to show d is proper and a monomorphism, hence a closed immersion. The new node 04XW is statement-only and self-contained; its affine-scheme test is equivalent to Stacks' quasi-compact-space test by 03HF. lean.statement: theorem separation_of_surjective_universallyClosed {S : Scheme.{u}} (X Y : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hsurj : Function.Surjective (mapPoint f.hom.hom)) (hclosed : MapIsUniversallyClosed f) : ((∀ (U V : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj) (b : yoneda.obj V ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsAffine U.left → IsAffine V.left → CompactSpace (Point (Limits.pullback a b))) → ∀ (U V : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ Y.obj.obj) (b : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y.obj.obj), IsAffine U.left → IsAffine V.left → CompactSpace (Point (Limits.pullback a b))) ∧ ((∀ (U V : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj) (b : yoneda.obj V ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsAffine U.left → IsAffine V.left → ∃ (W : Over S) (p : W ⟶ U) (q : W ⟶ V), IsPullback (yoneda.map p) (yoneda.map q) a b ∧ IsClosedImmersion (prod.lift p.left q.left)) → ∀ (U V : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ Y.obj.obj) (b : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y.obj.obj), IsAffine U.left → IsAffine V.left → ∃ (W : Over S) (p : W ⟶ U) (q : W ⟶ V), IsPullback (yoneda.map p) (yoneda.map q) a b ∧ IsClosedImmersion (prod.lift p.left q.left))
lean.note: Both independent absolute separation implications, using the equivalent affine-pair tests of Stacks 0AHR and 0AHS. The product in prod.lift p.left q.left is the absolute product of schemes over Spec Z, not the product in Over S. No base separation or representability of f is assumed.
